title: refactor: consolidate Stripe billing flow
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Extracts auto-top-up eligibility while preserving skip precedence, threshold behavior, reason strings, and pre-Stripe exits.
- Shares checkout-session Tinybird serialization across successful, failed, and expired checkout events.
- Preserves payment-status fallbacks, presentment fields, offered-method behavior, fulfillment, claim handling, and webhook acknowledgements.
- Adds combined regression coverage for auto-top-up skip paths and exact checkout event wire payloads.
- Supersedes #13749 and #13753.

Checks:
- Biome on all changed files
- Enter TypeScript typecheck
- `test/integration/stripe.test.ts` — 70/70 passed with checked-in test vars
- `git diff --check`

gist.headline: Stripe bees share a path
gist.blurb: The billing hive now sends checkout events down one well-tested path. Auto-top-ups still mind their thresholds, skip reasons, and all the tiny details that make money code politely terrifying.
gist.summary: Consolidated Stripe checkout-event serialization and auto-top-up eligibility logic while preserving payment-status fallbacks, presentment fields, fulfillment, claim handling, webhook acknowledgements, and existing skip/threshold behavior.
gist.impact: Checkout, payment, and auto-top-up flows keep the same user-visible behavior, now backed by shared logic and regression tests covering exact webhook payloads and skip paths.
gist.visual_concept: Polli, wearing a tiny accountant visor, tends a cozy garden of checkout receipts flowing through one shared irrigation pipe into a Stripe-like payment terminal. A CRT monitor robot carefully compares identical event slips while flowers grow from labeled auto-top-up pots, representing preserved thresholds and skip rules.
